body: Three specific problems. (1) The quantization model is physically underspecified in a way that determines the whole answer: FR-002/US-1 quantize over the signal's own amplitude range ('(max-min)/(2^N-1)'), making the quantization step size signal- and SNR-dependent. A real ADC has a fixed full-scale range set by the instrument, so the ratio of quantization noise to detector noise is a constant property of the digitizer, not something that varies with each injection. As specified, the experiment measures a different (and less physically meaningful) quantity — an adaptive-gain quantizer — and the resulting 'threshold SNR' would be an artifact of the chosen normalization. The spec never states whether a fixed ADC full-scale (with the signal possibly clipping or occupying a small fraction of range) or per-signal rescaling is intended, and the two choices give different answers. (2) The compute budget is not established: US-2 scenario 3 requires Bayesian parameter estimation (PyCBC-Inference/Bilby) on 'a set of 50 quantized signals' within 6 hours on a 2-core CPU. Full BBH parameter estimation typically takes hours per event even on tens of cores; 50 signals × 6 bit depths × float64 baselines × multiple SNR points × 10 independent runs (SC-005) is orders of magnitude beyond this budget, and nothing in the spec shows a reduced-dimensional sampler, fewer live points, or any other mechanism that would make the number credible. (3) Several load-bearing quantities are '[deferred]': the fraction of signals meeting the SNR range in US-1 scenario 1, the crossover threshold in US-3 scenario 1, and the number of signals per run in SC-005. Since SC-005's reproducibility criterion (std < 0.5 SNR units) depends directly on the deferred per-run sample count, the criterion cannot currently be evaluated for feasibility.
